subject: Spring transition: proposal to patch EU/US demo time gap
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Pieter van Dijk <pieter@eurocommerce.com>, Lucy Hayes <lucy@finbridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spring transition: proposal to patch EU/US demo time gap

Hi Pieter / Lucy,

Quick heads up: the US daylight-saving change (Mar 14) and the EU change (Mar 28) create a 2-week window where our usual demo times move relative to your local calendars. For EuroCommerce we currently run the deep-dive demo at 10:00 CET, which during that two-week period would land at 04:00 US ET / 01:00 PT — not great for either side.

Options I want to propose so we keep momentum without forcing inconvenient times:
- Option A: Move the demo earlier by 1 hour on the Euro side for the two-week window (9:00 CET) — keeps US folks between 05:00–08:00 ET.
- Option B: Run the live demo at 16:00 CET (late afternoon Europe) — this hits reasonable morning times in the US (10:00–11:00 ET).
- Option C: Split into two shorter sessions (EU-facing deep-dive + US-facing Q&A) and record the demo for anyone who can’t make it.

I attached a quick matrix with candidate slots across the two-week mismatch and a proposed rotation so we don’t over-index on any one timezone. Can you indicate which option you prefer (A/B/C) and which of the candidate dates on the sheet work?

Thanks — want to lock this before invites go out.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0164
[Attachment: regional_slots_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Pieter van Dijk <pieter@eurocommerce.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucy Hayes <lucy@finbridge.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Spring transition: proposal to patch EU/US demo time gap

Thanks Alex — helpful note.

Between the options, Option B (late afternoon CET) looks best for our leadership and the product team — they need to be fully present for the walkthrough. Option C could work if we kept the EU deep-dive first and the US Q&A later in the day.

For dates, earliest preferred is week of Mar 22 (we can do Tue 23 or Thu 25 after 15:00 CET). We’d rather avoid anything before Mar 22 because our execs are on travel the preceding week.

Best,
Pieter
Pieter van Dijk
Director of Integrations, EuroCommerce
[pieter@eurocommerce.com]

Alex — quick internal note. If we pick Option B we should ask engineering to have a lighter config for the first 20 minutes (reduced history) so model runtime is predictable for the cross-region audience — multi-region demos have shown token spikes at the high-load tail. I can own the engineering ask, Karthik can you schedule a short runthrough?

Also suggest we open a single calendar invite with two optional segments (Main demo 16:00–16:45 CET / Follow-up Q&A 17:00–17:30 CET) so attendees can opt into the slot that suits them.

— Vanessa

Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
